How do I get a student job with no experience?

Start with jobs that offer training, such as cafes, shops, events and school support. Show what you can already do: volunteering, clubs, sport, group projects and caring for family all count. Apply to several jobs at once, and apply early in the day, as many shifts are filled fast.
What should go on a student CV?

Keep it to one page. Put the days and hours you can work near the top, then your course, any work or volunteering, and two or three skills with a short example each. Use our free UK CV template to start.
What happens at a part-time job interview?

Most are short and friendly, often 15 to 20 minutes, sometimes with a trial shift. Expect questions about when you can work, how you would deal with a busy customer and why you want the job. Arrive a few minutes early and bring ID that shows your right to work.
When and how will I get paid?
Most part-time jobs pay weekly, every two weeks or monthly, straight into your bank account. You have a legal right to a payslip that shows your pay and any tax or National Insurance taken off.
Yes. Part-time, casual and zero-hours workers all build up paid holiday. Ask your employer how they work it out and how to book it.
Can I turn down shifts during exams?
On a zero-hours or casual contract you can usually say no to shifts. Tell your manager your exam dates early, and update the hours you can work when your timetable changes.
How do I spot a fake job?

Never pay for training, a uniform or a DBS check up front. Be careful if an employer only talks to you on WhatsApp or Telegram, offers very high pay for easy work, or asks for bank details before an interview.
How often are new student jobs added?
Every morning. Jobs older than 30 days, or that have closed, are taken off, so everything you see is current. Save the jobs you like so you can find them again.
